issues.description: image.tobytes() with format='RGB' silently corrupts non-RGB images returned by the model
issues.detail: PIL images from Gemini may arrive as RGBA, P, or L. Calling tobytes() without first converting and then asserting format='RGB' complects 'whatever PIL decoded' with 'what the downstream pipeline is told it received.' Make the conversion explicit: img = image.convert('RGB'); then push img.tobytes() with size and 'RGB'. One value, one mode, no hidden state.

issues.description: Mutating a third-party module's private global (genai._api_client.READ_BUFFER_SIZE) at import time
issues.detail: This is place-oriented programming at its worst: a process-wide mutation of a private attribute on someone else's module, executed as an import side effect, labeled 'temporary hack.' It complects 'import this service' with 'reconfigure the genai client globally for every consumer in the process.' Push it to construction time, document it, or upstream a fix.

issues.description: Model-capability dispatch encoded as substring checks on the model name
issues.detail: Two places now branch on startswith('gemini-2.5-flash') and 'image' in model_name. The model string is being asked to carry capability facts (supports-thinking, is-image-model) that should be values. Lift to a small data table keyed by model id returning a capability record; the branches become lookups.

issues.description: Default model change is a behavior shift smuggled into a feature PR
issues.detail: Flipping the default from gemini-2.0-flash to gemini-2.5-flash changes time semantics, cost, and latency for every existing caller who relied on the default. It is noted in CHANGELOG but complected with an unrelated image-generation feature. Separate concerns: ship as its own change so users can reason about the value of 'default' independently.

issues.description: Image part handled inline inside a deep candidate/part loop instead of as a value transformation
issues.detail: The new elif sits beside text and function-call handling, each doing its own push_frame. The loop is accreting concerns. A small pure function part_to_frame(part) -> Frame|None would decompose 'what is this part' from 'when do we emit it,' and make image, text, and tool-call paths symmetric and testable without mocks.

issues.description: No bounds on returned image size despite a 5MB read buffer bump
issues.detail: The 5MB buffer is raised to accept large images, but nothing downstream validates size or dimensions before decoding with PIL and pushing into the pipeline. That is essential complexity (untrusted-ish bytes, decoder, memory) being treated as easy. Make the size and format explicit values and reject what does not fit.

review.summary: The feature is small and the diff is mostly mechanical, but it imports two classic complectings: a global mutation of a third-party module's private buffer size at import time, and capability dispatch encoded as substring checks on a model-name string. Both are EASY-NOT-SIMPLE and PLACE-ORIENTED. The image-emission path also conflates 'whatever PIL decoded' with a declared 'RGB' format, which will silently produce wrong bytes for RGBA/P/L returns. Finally, the default-model change is a behavior shift complected with a feature; it belongs in its own commit so callers can reason about the value of 'default' separately. Decompose: explicit conversion before tobytes, capability table keyed by model id, push buffer config to client construction, and a small part_to_frame value-returning helper.
